clue.text: Confound fat Herbert, full of wind!

parts.note: flab is excess body fat

indicators.note: Herbert's short name is full of, i.e. wraps round, the word for wind

parts.note: Bert is the usual short form of the name Herbert
gas is wind in the stomach

explanation.surface: A command to bewilder some portly, windbag fellow called Herbert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts the wind inside Herbert's short name; the exclamation mark only adds to the comic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To flabbergast someone is to astonish and baffle them, a synonym of confound.

clue.text: Escape with king on south side of meadow

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece on the south side sits below, so it comes after the meadow word

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch flees by slipping out along the bottom edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on south side of' puts K below LEA in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is an escape of liquid or gas, or of secret information.

clue.text: Former PM upset labour with initial ferocity

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disarranged, so the letters are reshuffled
the initial of a word is its first letter, here of ferocity

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister who angered the Labour party with fierce early attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles LABOUR together with F, the first letter given by 'initial ferocity'. Arthur Balfour was a Conservative British Prime Minister (1902-05).
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour served as British Prime Minister from 1902 to 1905, so he is a past premier.

clue.text: Poet's heading off to get food

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken off here

parts.note: John Keats was an English Romantic poet; the 's is part of his name as written

explanation.surface: A poet sets off to find something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes K, the first letter of KEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for meals or grub, a noun meaning nourishment.

clue.text: Fellow at home keeps a flowering plant

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow

indicators.note: the word for at home keeps, i.e. holds, the letter a inside it

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A man staying in looks after a plant in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts the A inside the word for at home; 'Fellow' and 'at home' read as a domestic scene, not as separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are alpine plants grown for their vivid blue trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Cut tail off bird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, which is cut off here

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: An instruction to dock a bird's tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' drops E, the last letter of SNIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors.

clue.text: Coming out, slack drones became united in common purpose

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerge in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lazy male bees emerge from the hive and band together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' rearranges SLACK and DRONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To close ranks is an idiom for a group standing together to defend itself.

clue.text: What a game taking pills — roughly nine swallowed!

indicators.note: the pills word swallows, i.e. takes inside it, the scrambled nine

parts.note: tablets are pills

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or messily, so the letters of nine are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a sporting contest in which a player gulps down about nine pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' jumbles the letters of nine and 'swallowed' places them inside the pills; 'What a' is exclamatory padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is an indoor bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: Eating grass and rodent is a very good thing for this old creature

indicators.note: the very good thing is eating, i.e. has inside it, the grass and the rodent

parts.note: something that is the tops is the very best
rice is a cereal grass
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Grazing grass and rodents is said to suit some prehistoric animal very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' places the grass and the rodent inside the very good thing; 'the tops' is informal for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Triceratops was a three-horned dinosaur, a creature from the distant past.

clue.text: Silly oaf arrives and I must show social graces

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are behaving foolishly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: A clumsy lout turns up and I must model good manners for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges OAF, ARRIVES and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoir faire is French for knowing how to act, the poise and tact of polished society.

clue.text: Once again on the battle line the wrong way round

parts.note: back means once again, as in 'back in business'
to can mean on or against, as in 'face to face' or 'put the door to'
the front is the line where armies meet in battle

explanation.surface: A soldier returns to the front line, and the whole scene seems inverted.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to front describes something reversed, with its rear facing forward.

clue.text: Bird left Noah's boat

parts.note: the ark was the vessel Noah built for the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird flew off from Noah's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, famed for singing as it rises.

clue.text: Soldier's piece of writing

definitions.meaning: a member of a parachute regiment
short for paragraph, a section of text

explanation.surface: A soldier's essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper is called a para, and the same clipping stands for a paragraph of text.

clue.text: Old instrument consisting of large bag only

parts.note: a sack is a large bag
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: An antique instrument that is nothing more than a big bag, like bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut was a Renaissance brass instrument, an early form of trombone.

clue.text: Old lover given external wallop, one in a state

indicators.note: the wallop word is given to the old lover as an outer layer, i.e. placed round it

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat or wallop them
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A former partner takes an outside thrashing and ends up in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given external' wraps the wallop round the former lover. 'In a state' suggests being upset; here it means living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Texan is a native or resident of Texas, one of the United States.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical garment making kneeler in church cold, not hot

indicators.note: the phrase 'cold, not hot' says the cold letter appears where the hot one was

parts.note: a hassock is a cushion for kneeling on in church
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Making a kneeling cushion into a garment by switching the heating off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' signals swapping H in HASSOCK for C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is a long robe worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: What's concerning a city even after revolution

indicators.note: the word stays the same, even when it is turned round end to end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something municipal stays level even after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even after revolution' says the answer reads the same both ways; 'revolution' misleads towards politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a town or its citizens and municipal affairs.

clue.text: Sticky stuff, sealant initially holds strap together

indicators.note: the sealant's first letter holds the strap together, sitting inside it as a clasp

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to guide a horse

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of sealant

explanation.surface: A gluey sealant is applied first so it binds a strap together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S, and 'holds' with 'together' says S sits inside REIN, joining its halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a gummy substance produced by trees and used in varnish and glue.

clue.text: Bogarde's potentially lethal weapon

definitions.meaning: Bogarde's first name: the British film star Sir ... Bogarde
a dagger, especially a Scottish one, is a weapon that can kill

explanation.surface: An actor's dangerous weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirk Bogarde was a British film actor, and a dirk is a long Highland dagger.

clue.text: Second-rate foreign city, but it shows vivacity

parts.note: B grade means second-rate
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

explanation.surface: A second-class city abroad nevertheless has plenty of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is an Italian-derived word for liveliness and verve.

clue.text: Criticise independent Conservative responsible for alarm

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Attacking a maverick Tory who caused a scare.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, the same as alarm.

clue.text: Old city's ceremony attended by leaders of each individual institution

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, taken from each, individual and institution

explanation.surface: An ancient city's pageant attended by the heads of every single institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes the first letters of the last three words. Pompeii was the Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was a Roman town near Naples, destroyed by a volcanic eruption.

clue.text: Company board reshuffled in Spanish city

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorganises, so the letters of board are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm reorganises its directors in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffled' signals the anagram of board, read as a company's directors in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordoba is a city in Andalusia, famous for its great mosque.

clue.text: Changed at once after first glimpse of Artemis — into a stag!

definitions.text: Changed at once after first glimpse of Artemis — into a stag!

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the Artemis letter
the first glimpse of a word is its opening letter, here of Artemis
changed means altered, so the letters of at once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter is instantly turned into a stag the moment he catches sight of the goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' turns AT ONCE into CTAEON, which comes 'after' A. In myth Actaeon saw the goddess Artemis bathing and she changed him into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon was the Greek hunter transformed into a deer for seeing Artemis naked.

clue.text: Pirate said to give uncouth impression

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: coarse air: coarse means uncouth and an air is an impression or manner

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is reputed to come across as rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' signals the sound of 'coarse air'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a privateer, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Old record held by knight in store

indicators.note: the old record is held by, i.e. contained within, the knight abbreviation

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format

explanation.surface: A vintage disc is kept safe by a knight in a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts the old record inside the knight abbreviation; Kt rather than the chess N is the knight here.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept means stored or reserved, so things kept are held in store.

clue.text: Drop bolt

definitions.meaning: a drop of water from the eye when crying
to bolt is to dash off at speed, to rush

explanation.surface: Lower the bar on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a drop, and to tear along is to bolt or race.

clue.text: Achievement walkers reported?

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: feet are what we walk with

explanation.surface: An accomplishment attributed to hikers in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that the word for walkers sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable accomplishment requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: Healthy food carrying stigma for the most part

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it but the last letter

parts.note: a brand is a mark of disgrace, a stigma

explanation.surface: A wholesome food carries a mark of shame, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops D from BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain, valued as dietary fibre.

clue.text: Computer group consisting of some slobby technicians

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A team of untidy IT workers makes up a computer group.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition also took 'consisting', but 'consisting of' is the link joining definition to wordplay; the definition is 'Computer group'.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is a set of eight bits processed by a computer as a unit.

clue.text: Agree to have a tête-à-tête?

definitions.meaning: to share the same opinion as someone
a tête-à-tête is a face-to-face private talk, so the parties literally look straight at each other

explanation.surface: Being of one mind when having an intimate chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing eye to eye is an idiom for agreeing, and literally describes two people facing each other closely.

clue.text: Support trainees working out hard problem

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: working out suggests the letters being exercised into a new shape

explanation.surface: Gym trainees who are working out find a tough challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' signals rearranging trainees, though the surface pictures them at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain teaser is a puzzle or riddle that is hard to solve.
